SMTO-HTTP-0065 — The web address in this request isn't valid

GUID: 1a39b308-beaa-404e-9ef6-d6ecff35e590
Slug: http-url-invalid
Domain: HTTP · Subsystem: http

What happened

  • SMTO couldn't use the web address for this request. It may be missing https://, contain spaces or odd characters, or be far too long. Nothing was sent.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Check the address you gave the Agent: it should start with https:// (or http://), contain no spaces, and use forward slashes (/). SMTO only sends requests to complete, well-formed web addresses.
  2. If the request uses a saved connection, open it in Parameter Store and check that Base URL is a complete address such as https://example.com. Short paths in a request are added to the Base URL, so a broken Base URL breaks every request.
  3. Keep passwords and keys out of the address; put them in the connection's Authentication section instead. Addresses can appear in logs and history, while the Authentication section keeps secrets protected.

What success looks like

  • The Agent's request is sent and returns a result from the service.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, together with the address you meant to use, to the person who manages SMTO.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • URL validation rejected the endpoint: it is missing or over 8 KiB, contains control characters, spaces, a backslash or a malformed percent-escape, is not http or https, or has an invalid host or port.

What this means

  • URL validation rejects a missing/oversized/malformed HTTP(S) address, invalid host/port, userinfo, control characters, backslash or a prohibited secret-bearing query. The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.

Why this can happen

  • URL validation rejects a missing/oversized/malformed HTTP(S) address, invalid host/port, userinfo, control characters, backslash or a prohibited secret-bearing query.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the URL's public structure and keep private values out of diagnostic copies.

How to fix it

  • Supply an absolute http(s) URL, or a path relative to the connection's base_url, with a valid hostname or IP, a port from 1 to 65535, percent-encoded spaces and no backslashes or control characters. Keep credentials in the connection's auth fields rather than in the URL.
  • Correct the endpoint URL. Store credentials in dedicated authentication fields and keep secrets out of URLs.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The resolved intended HTTP(S) URL passes structure and credential-location checks.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
